D.t: Everett Wess trails by 17.1 and wins 1% of simulations. Closing it takes about 146,538 voters switching sides, or 293,076 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +25.3 and R +9.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +14.8. Your best recent poll is Cygnal (R) for Gray Media and Alabama Daily News at R +13.8; your worst is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 73,882 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 34,692 votes; Madison, a projected net 10,012 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +6.9, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, R +1.0, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, R +1.2, 3.9% of the vote; Chambers, R +10.9, 0.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Everett Wess runs furthest behind in Cullman, Blount, Walker. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 68% of voters, 40 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.38 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 40 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.16 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 48 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.95 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Everett Wess: Immigration voters 14 to 85, White voters 30 to 69, Voters who can afford daily costs 33 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18K cash against $627K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $16.8M helping Barry Moore and $0 helping Everett Wess.
